missing: Deterministic port-0 listeners (docs/GO.md 'ports' control: 10000-29999 from the test's stream) do not work for TCP on Go 1.24+ when the kernel supports MPTCP: net.Listen goes through listenMPTCP -> listenTCPProto and bypasses the patched listenTCP, so httptest servers and net.Listen(":0") get kernel-random ports that differ run to run.
evidence: m3 TestNetLoopback, Go 1.24.7, /proc/sys/net/mptcp/enabled=1: two --det runs => httptest url 127.0.0.1:42345 vs :34033, listen0 :46311 vs :45041; with GODEBUG=multipathtcp=0 both runs give :24763/:15040. go/internal/overlay/overlay.go:124 patches only listenTCP; GOROOT/src/net/mptcpsock_linux.go:79 calls listenTCPProto directly (engine@release-1)

missing: The verifier reports 'covered by Level 0' / identical fingerprints for tests whose observed inputs differed between two --det runs (listener ports, raw clock, child-process entropy, file mtime second, TZ/LANG/env values): uncontrolled sources emit no event, so a difference in them is invisible to the fingerprint and verify cannot name it.
evidence: m3: det1 vs det3 OBS lines differ (ports, gettimeofday_sec, new file mtime 2024-12-31T23:59:59Z vs 2025-01-01T00:00:00Z, child sh/python random) yet `fenvix-go verify t1.jsonl t3.jsonl` => 'covered by Level 0: 18  not covered: 0'; same for t1 vs t2 run with TZ=Asia/Tokyo LANG=it_IT FOO=bar

missing: --det does not control or pin environment variables: the test sees the caller's whole environment (os.Getenv/os.Environ), and the values are neither normalised nor recorded as events in the trace.
evidence: m3 TestEnvIdentity under --det: plain env => FOO="" nenv=194; with FOO=bar => FOO="bar" nenv=197; verify of the two traces => identical. No env control in overlay.DetControls (go/internal/overlay/overlay.go:53, engine@release-1)

missing: --det does not fix the time zone: TZ and /etc/localtime pass through, so time.Local and formatted times differ between machines under --det.

missing: --det does not fix the locale (LANG/LC_*): values pass through to the test and to child processes and are not recorded.

missing: os.Hostname is not controlled under --det (the real machine name reaches the test), although the pid is virtualised with a PID namespace; no UTS namespace.

missing: --det silently forces GOMAXPROCS=1 for every test binary; a test asserting on runtime.GOMAXPROCS(0) > 1, or needing real parallelism (two goroutines spinning concurrently), sees 1. The forced value is only visible in the trace header and --help text, not printed at start.

missing: The mtime of a file written during a test is not deterministic under --det: it is the kernel's coarse real timestamp plus an offset, so it lands before or after the virtual 'now' depending on real timing (seen as 2024-12-31T23:59:59Z in one run and 2025-01-01T00:00:00Z in the next), and no event records it.

missing: The default virtual epoch is 2025-01-01, almost two years before today (2026-11-20), and exploration epochs stay inside 2025: any test comparing time.Now with a fixture created after the epoch (a certificate's NotBefore, a JWT iat/nbf, 'year >= 2026') fails under --det and passes plain. missing: Under --det t.Parallel is a no-op, so parallel subtests that must overlap (a barrier, a rendezvous over a channel, a shared server started by one and used by another) fail or time out; the test passes under plain go test. No hint is printed naming --det-keep-parallel.

missing: The one-P scheduler without preemption hides data races instead of reproducing them: an unsynchronised counter test that fails under plain go test (lost updates) passes every time under --det, so the flaky test is not turned into a reproducible defect and the bug is reported as absent.

missing: Go's own -shuffle=on|N is silently dropped under --det (the order is --det-seed's); no message tells the user their flag was ignored, and a seed printed by an earlier plain `go test -shuffle` failure ('-test.shuffle 1700000000') cannot be replayed under --det.

missing: -count=N under --det runs each test N times with the same seed and writes N trace records with the same node id; verify then counts them as one test (last record wins), so a repetition that diverges or fails can be masked, and -count cannot be used to hunt a flake under --det.

missing: With -trimpath the hooks no longer recognise the standard library (file paths lose the GOROOT prefix): every event's site becomes fenvix's own overlay file (time/zz_fenvix.go:79) instead of the user's file:line, and package testing's own clock reads are taken for the test's (they tick the virtual clock and enter the fingerprint; reported durations become virtual).

missing: With -cover, skip with proof never reuses anything: go test sets GOCOVERDIR to a fresh temp dir per run and the key treats it as an input, so every test reruns with reason env:GOCOVERDIR.

missing: With -coverprofile, skip with proof never reuses anything: the binary's -test.coverprofile argument is a per-run temp path and is keyed, so every test reruns with reason code-or-config. decide_for: 1.21 is below the stated floor (1.22+) and end of life

missing: The first --det or skip run on each toolchain rebuilds the whole standard library under the overlay (and every dependency): 21-59 s for an 8-test module here. It is kept only in GOCACHE, so a CI job without a persisted Go build cache pays it on every run; nothing prebuilds or ships it.

missing: Skip mode without --det does not control randomness, map order or scheduling, yet reuses a pass 'with proof': a test that passes half the time is frozen as PASS after its first lucky run and never fails again until an input changes. missing: Skip mode runs every test at 'today 00:00 UTC + elapsed': a test that fails now on the real clock (a fixture that expired at 01:00 today, a time-of-day rule) passes in a fresh fenvix run and is reused all day; only --skip-real-clock shows it.
evidence: m5/d TestNotAfterOneAM at 08:51 UTC: plain go test => FAIL 'expired'; `fenvix-go test --skip-cache=.scd` => PASS then 'reused with proof'; `--skip-real-clock` => '1 passed on the virtual day and fail on the real clock' exit 1. Recorded in brain DECISIONS.md:19 (2026-11-19) and docs/GO.md:68
decide_for: DECISIONS 2026-11-19: with the real clock Go skip reused 3-15% of test time vs 37-64% for Go's own cache; the day is keyed and a nightly real-clock run bounds the delay to one day
decide_against: a fresh (not reused) fenvix run reports PASS where go test fails right now; the promise is 'never a wrong reuse' and the nightly check is not a delivered product piece (next entry)

missing: The nightly real-clock check that bounds the virtual-day trade-off is not delivered to customers: it is a flag (--skip-real-clock) plus a workflow in the engine's own repository; the customer must write and schedule their own cron job and restore the same cache. No Action, no service run, no report surface.
evidence: .github/workflows/go-nightly-real-clock.yml exists only in the engine repo (engine@release-1); docs/GO.md:68 'Run it nightly in CI, for example a GitHub Actions job with on: schedule ...'

missing: The whole environment is one key ('env:*') as soon as a test starts a program with the default environment or calls os.Environ: any variable that changes (GitHub's GITHUB_RUN_ID, GITHUB_SHA, RUNNER_* change on every CI run) reruns that test and every later test of the package. The harness walks ran all commits inside one job, so measured reuse does not show this.

missing: Prefix rule: one changed input reruns the dependent test and every test after it in the same package, although they did not read it.

missing: No per-test code dependency for Go: the code key is the whole test binary, so a change to any function linked into a package's test binary (the package or anything it imports) reruns every test of that package, exactly like Go's own cache. Per-test reuse exists only for non-code inputs.
evidence: m4 probe 'lib-used' (lib.Value changed, used by one test TestOtherPkg): all 19 tests of package p rerun with why 'code-or-config'; exec.go:206 static key 'bin' = binaryContentID; docs/GO.md:63

missing: Changing build flags (-tags) reruns every package, including packages with no tag-dependent file whose test binary is unchanged: the flags are in the static key next to the binary content.
